items.stem: Under California wage-and-hour rules, a nonexempt employee works a 10-hour day. How is daily overtime generally treated differently from the federal standard?

options.text: California generally requires overtime after 8 hours in a workday, not only after 40 in a week
options.rationale: Correct: California applies daily overtime after 8 hours, which federal law does not require.

options.text: California never requires overtime if weekly hours stay under 40
options.rationale: Incorrect: daily overtime can apply even when the weekly total is under 40.

options.text: California applies the same 40-hour-only rule as federal law
options.rationale: Incorrect: California adds a daily overtime standard beyond the weekly federal rule.

options.text: California prohibits any work beyond 8 hours per day
options.rationale: Incorrect: longer days are permitted with appropriate overtime, not prohibited.

items.explanation: Correct: California applies daily overtime after 8 hours, which federal law does not require.

items.stem: A California employer wants to classify a worker as an independent contractor. Which framework is most associated with that determination in California?

options.text: An 'ABC'-style test that presumes employee status unless specific conditions are met
options.rationale: Correct: California commonly applies an ABC-style test that presumes employment unless the criteria are satisfied.

options.text: A rule that any worker who signs a contractor agreement is automatically a contractor
options.rationale: Incorrect: a signed agreement does not by itself establish contractor status.

options.text: A rule based solely on whether the worker is paid by invoice
options.rationale: Incorrect: payment method alone does not determine classification.

options.text: A rule that part-time workers are always contractors
options.rationale: Incorrect: part-time status does not determine contractor classification.

items.explanation: Correct: California commonly applies an ABC-style test that presumes employment unless the criteria are satisfied.

items.stem: Select TWO characteristics of California's Fair Employment and Housing Act (FEHA) that commonly differ from the federal baseline.

options.text: It applies to employers with fewer employees than some federal thresholds
options.rationale: Correct: FEHA's coverage reaches smaller employers than some federal statutes.

options.text: It recognizes protected categories beyond the minimum federal list
options.rationale: Correct: California recognizes additional protected characteristics beyond the federal baseline.

options.text: It eliminates the need for any anti-harassment training
options.rationale: Incorrect: California expands, rather than eliminates, harassment-prevention training duties.

options.text: It removes all recordkeeping obligations for employers
options.rationale: Incorrect: FEHA does not remove recordkeeping obligations.

options.text: It applies only to public-sector employers
options.rationale: Incorrect: FEHA applies broadly to private and public employers.

items.explanation: Correct: FEHA's coverage reaches smaller employers than some federal statutes.
